bites.headline: Course Introduction
bites.body: Professor Kagan introduces the course and the material that will be covered during the semester.

bites.headline: Keep this bit
bites.body: He aims to clarify what the class will focus on in particular and which subjects it will steer away from.

bites.headline: The Nature of Persons: Dualism vs. Physicalism
bites.body: Professor Kagan discusses the two main positions with regard to the question, "What is a person?" On the one hand, there is the dualist view, according to which a person is a body and a soul.

bites.headline: Keep this bit
bites.body: On the other hand, the physicalist view argues that a person is just a body.

bites.headline: Arguments for the Existence of the Soul, Part I
bites.body: The lecture focuses on arguments that might be offered as proof for the existence of the soul.

bites.headline: Keep this bit
bites.body: The first series of arguments discussed is those known as "inferences to the best explanation." That is, we posit the existence of things we cannot see so as to explain something else that is generally agreed to take place.
